rubrics.criterion: The local-mode authorizer entry point is decomposed so that its distinct responsibilities -- route lookup against the registered routes, credential/token interpretation (including the JWT payload handling with its padding of short urlsafe segments), authorizer-event translation, and policy verification against the method ARN -- are each performed by their own appropriately scoped, individually reviewable unit (method, function, or equivalent callable), and the entry reads as a short sequence of such units rather than one body holding all of them. Any equivalent decomposition (different names, different number of units, or one unit covering adjacent sub-steps coherently) satisfies this as long as no leftover unit still holds several unrelated stages verbatim.
rubrics.rationale: This instance's first manifestation absorbs a three-level helper chain (route resolution -> JWT/claims interpretation -> event translation -> policy verification) into the authorizer entry; crediting its resolution requires observing that the four conceptually distinct stages are separately scoped again, not that any particular original helper name returns.

rubrics.criterion: The local-mode request serving entry point is decomposed so that Lambda-context construction, the Lambda-event synthesis (route matching plus header casing, query-parameter parity handling, and binary content-type detection with base64 encoding), the unmatched-route ForbiddenError translation, and the OPTIONS/CORS preflight handling are each their own appropriately scoped unit, and the entry reads as a short sequence of such units. Any equivalent decomposition satisfies this as long as no one method keeps the whole request pipeline verbatim.
rubrics.rationale: The second local-mode manifestation absorbs the event-synthesis and preflight factory chain into the request entry; the semantic outcome is that request translation and preflight are individually reviewable again.

rubrics.criterion: The typed AWS client's Lambda function-update path is decomposed so that the code-update stage (including its retry/error-context handling and the function-updated waiter), the configuration-payload assembly stage (including VPC rebuilding and the retry wrapper), and the tag-reconciliation stage (listing remote tags, removing unrequested ones, then applying new/differing ones) are each their own appropriately scoped unit, and the public update entry reads as a short sequence of these stages. Any equivalent stage decomposition is acceptable; the shared function ARN and client/waiter context may be threaded or owned by whichever unit the repair chooses.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation absorbs the deploy client's three-step code/config/tags pipeline verbatim into one method; resolution means the three deploy stages are separately scoped, not that the original private helper names or parameter shapes are restored.

rubrics.criterion: The SAM websocket API template generation is decomposed so that producing the handler integrations with their invoke permissions, creating the per-route entries (including connect/disconnect/default integration targeting), rendering the optional custom-domain and api-mapping resources, and assembling the template Outputs are each performed by appropriately scoped units, and the generator entry reads as a short sequence of section-producing units. Any equivalent sectioning is acceptable, including units shared with or parallel to the Terraform generator only if behavior is preserved.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation absorbs five SAM template-section writers into one generator entry; credit requires each template section to be produced by its own scoped unit again, without prescribing the original section writer boundaries.

rubrics.criterion: The redeploy resource sweeper is decomposed so that plan indexing (mapping recorded resources by name), per-resource-type staleness comparison (name absence plus per-type external-identity comparison for the bucket/topic/queue/stream/stream-arn cases and the per-key api-mapping comparison for custom domains), and deletion planning (handler selection, argument preparation, and append-vs-insert plan placement) are each appropriately scoped units, and the sweep entry reads as a short sequence of such units. Per-type comparisons may be dispatched, tabulated, or branched in any form as long as each resource type's comparison is its own reviewable unit.
rubrics.rationale: This manifestation absorbs the sweeper's mark/diff/plan chain including the collapsed dynamic dispatch family; resolution means the sweep is again composed of scoped units, while the dispatch mechanism itself is a free design choice.

rubrics.criterion: No solving-unit merely relocates an absorbed pipeline: the five entry paths above (local-mode authorization, local-mode request serving, the Lambda function update, SAM websocket generation, redeploy sweeping) must not end in opaque wrappers whose helper bodies contain an entire former pipeline as an unreadable mass, and no pipeline was cut into arbitrary fragments that do not correspond to its actual stages (for example, splitting a body at a fixed position and threading a dozen locals through the seam).
rubrics.rationale: Moving a monolithic body behind one giant helper, or fragmenting it at mechanical boundaries, changes call counts without restoring named stages; both are known evasions of this smell's resolution and are graded against resolution here.

rubrics.criterion: All re-extracted units are wired into their caller's execution path: the sweeper's execution walks still consult the re-scoped staleness comparisons for every applicable deployed resource (including api-mapping entries named as compound keys), deletion planning still reaches its handlers through whatever dispatch the repair chose, and no newly scoped unit exists unreferenced while its logic is duplicated elsewhere in the caller.
rubrics.rationale: Re-extraction only counts if the re-created units are actually used by the sweep path; shadow copies of the comparisons left inline would duplicate responsibilities the case is about.

rubrics.criterion: The local-mode request/authorization state threading is preserved across the new unit boundaries: the request event and context objects produced by upstream units are the same objects consulted and mutated by downstream units (route resolution results feed event synthesis; token claims and authorizer results feed the auth-context update; policy verdicts feed the admit/deny decision), without re-implementing per-unit copies or private re-derivations that can drift.
rubrics.rationale: The inlined bodies shared one mutable request state; a decomposition that loses that sharing (or duplicates event/context assembly between units) breaks the request pipeline the way a mechanical split would.

rubrics.criterion: The function-update stages continue to share their execution context: the function ARN obtained from the code-update stage is the one the tag reconciliation runs against, waiter synchronization and the retry wrapper remain bound to the specific client calls that need them, and error-context construction for code-update failures still reports the same operation and payload facts.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed pipeline passes the ARN and client state between its three stages; a repair that loses the shared context (re-listing, re-deriving, or tagging a stale/different ARN) changes deploy behavior even when each stage looks reasonable in isolation.

rubrics.criterion: The re-scoped websocket template sections emit into the same single template structure under the same presence conditions: integrations and invoke permissions exist exactly for the handler entries present in the template, per-handler output keys exist exactly for present handlers, and the domain/mapping resources exist only when a domain is declared.
rubrics.rationale: Section re-extraction must keep the conditional wiring of the SAM template; emitting sections unconditionally or against different presence checks would change generated templates for real apps.

rubrics.criterion: No bridging leftovers from the inlined bodies survive: intermediate variables that existed only to carry absorbed stage state inside an entry method, unused locals introduced mid-body, or dead assignment branches are absent once the stages are re-scoped; every variable named in the changed methods is either used by the unit that declares it or deliberately returned/threaded to a caller that uses it.
rubrics.rationale: Mechanical extraction commonly leaves the stitching state behind; this instance's absorbed bodies introduced stage locals per absorbed helper, so leftovers are observable and instance-specific.

rubrics.criterion: No comment that narrates or rationalizes a collapsed call chain remains attached to the re-decomposed methods: prose asserting that an update sequence is 'kept in one place' or 'splitting these stages apart tends to obscure' (or any equivalent chain-internal-stage narration that no longer matches the structure) is not left in place next to code that has been re-scoped.
rubrics.rationale: The case's terminal-state bodies carry comments defending their own bulk; after a genuine re-decomposition those explanations are factually wrong, and their persistence signals the structure was left in place or only cosmetically rearranged.

rubrics.criterion: No unused imports or module-level type aliases remain in the changed modules as a result of the re-decomposition: names that were only referenced by the absorbed bodies are either still referenced by the re-scoped units in the same module or removed, and the repair does not leave a moved-unit's helper stranded in a module nothing imports.
rubrics.rationale: The affected modules (local-mode machinery, the AWS deploy client, SAM generation, the sweeper) carry module-level aliases the inlined bodies referenced; cleanup of those edges is part of moving the code back out.

rubrics.criterion: The duplicated inline assembly regions that pasting produced are given a single ownership: in particular the two verbatim copies of the auth-context construction/update (claims/principal into the request's authorizer context) inside the local-mode authorization entry are not re-emitted as two separate but identical copies; one scoped unit may serve both producing paths (equivalent consolidations are fine).
rubrics.rationale: This instance specifically pasted the auth-context update at each of its two producing paths instead of calling one shared unit; that duplication is an artifact of the inlining being modeled, and both grading and review treat duplicate logic left behind as unresolved.

rubrics.criterion: Generated SAM templates are unchanged for equivalent applications: identical resource keys and properties, the same route/deployment DependsOn wiring, the same integration and invoke-permission content, the same optional domain/mapping resources, and the same websocket Outputs content (API id, per-handler ARN and name outputs with the documented key spelling, and the endpoint URL interpolation over the stage).
rubrics.rationale: The SAM generation site is behavior-critical: template parity for existing websocket apps is the observable contract that a re-sectioned generator must not disturb, and it is testable against fixtures in the shipped suite.

rubrics.criterion: Local-mode request behavior is preserved: the translated event keeps its documented semantics (lowercased headers, query-parameter parity including the None case, binary handling that base64-encodes bodies of binary content types and sets the encoded flag), OPTIONS preflight responses still allow exactly the methods the views declare with the CORS headers Chalice generates, and authorization denial still produces the same 401/403 error payloads (message wording, error-type header values) and the same treatment of unpadded JWT payload segments.
rubrics.rationale: These are the locally observable behaviors of the two local-mode manifestations; plausible wrong repairs (dropping the encoded flag, guessing CORS methods, re-quoting the JWT, dropping the padding fallback) regresses the local testing story this code exists for.

rubrics.criterion: Function-update transactionality is preserved: configuration keys are sent only for provided values with VPC config rebuilt so omitted values detach the function from the VPC, the update call still tolerates a function settling from a previous deployment (waiter/retry placement before or after the relevant update calls as required by the shipped behavior), tags are reconciled in the same order effect (unrequested remote tags removed before requested ones are applied), and code-update failures still raise errors carrying the same operation/payload context.
rubrics.rationale: The absorbed stages encode deploy-critical sequencing; a repair that reorders waiter/retry or rewrites the tag reconciliation changes what a redeploy does to a live function.

rubrics.criterion: Sweeper detection semantics are unchanged: only deployed entries the new plan does not reference are flagged, name-absence still falls out, external-identity comparisons for s3 bucket and the topic/queue/stream/stream-arn event sources compare exactly the same data, domain-name cleanup still targets only api-mapping keys absent from the new plan (per-key granularity), and a resource type the sweeper does not know how to handle still raises the error at execution time.
rubrics.rationale: Sweep misses delete user resources or orphan them (destructive both ways); the per-type comparison data and the unknown-type error are the observable semantics of the absorbed comparator family.

rubrics.criterion: The resulting deploy plan is structurally the same: deletion instructions still run in reverse creation order, api-mapping deletions are still inserted at the front of the plan, instruction/message bookkeeping still attaches each message to the instruction it belongs to, and the exact client call parameters (method names and parameter keys) produced for each removed resource are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: Deletion ordering and front-insertion are load-bearing for custom domains; the sweeper manifestation's absorbed planning loop is exactly the code that guarantees them.
